text: Throw recon bolt where a teammate can already shoot into the scan, information nobody is positioned to act on is wasted utility.
Fire recon bolt high above an enemy wall rather than into it, the scan clears the wall and you can spam through it for free damage.
An instant recon bolt off the barrier is a pro habit built on a coordinated space take, alone it just scans an empty corner and leaves you blind later.
Rotate with recon bolt still up, arriving somewhere new with it already spent turns the rotate into a blind fight.
Half a second early and recon bolt scans the corner behind them, wait for the contact before you fire it.
Sova anchors a site as well as he rotates, a scan above a push is just as strong from a hold as it is on the move.
Hunter's fury needs runway, back up as you cast so you have room to sweep, walking forward while you ult throws away most of the angle.
Entry in checkpoints, take one piece of space, survive behind cover, then wait for the team to reach you before you take the next.
Do not move to the next piece of space before your team reaches the last one, you are the fastest player there and they cannot trade what they cannot reach.
Sitting far up forces them to respect you, watch the minimap and punish the moment they overstep toward the rest of your team.
The agent you picked does not decide whether you are allowed to flank or take space, that is a choice about the round, not about your role.
Never stand still while holding an angle, small steps in and out beat a static crosshair because they have to find you again every time.
Burst, move, burst, move, the kills come from being hard to hit as much as from the first bullet landing.
You accelerate from a standstill in this game, so hugging the wall you are about to peek means you arrive slowly and get shot first.
Step off the wall and build your speed before the corner, so the peek is fast instead of a slow lean into their crosshair.
Do not walk straight out of a smoke in a straight line, angle the exit so they have to move their crosshair to find you.
Decide how you are taking an angle before you arrive at it, the way you pick the lane before the turn, hesitating at the corner is what gets you traded.
Scoping a rifle roots you in place, take the angle unscoped and keep moving unless the range genuinely demands it.
Bucky does 17 a pellet inside 8 meters, 13 past that and 9 past 12, so hold where they arrive close, never the long angle.
Judge does 17 a pellet inside 10 meters, 10 past that and 7 past 15, so its whole value is the close re peek.
Aim a shotgun at body height rather than head height, a headshot level crosshair sends most of the pellets straight over them.
Phantom does 39 to the body inside 20 meters and 35 past it, so a long hold costs you a fifth bullet the Vandal never needs.
Two or three stars placed before the round is the sweet spot, none leaves you slow and all five leaves you nothing to answer a rotate with.
Nova pulse low and gravity well high pulls them up into the open with nothing to hide behind, the pair is worth far more than either alone.
Smoke the same spot every round until they walk into it on trust, then pull it back and take the kills they hand you.
When your team commits, get the smoke down fast and get back on your gun, a perfect smoke that lands after the entry is a wasted round.
A shallow smoke beats a deep one, it leaves them exposed to every angle as they step out instead of letting them isolate just one.
Gun in hand is the priority, utility is how you win the fight, not something you do instead of taking it.
Force an operator to play the retake rather than the peek, hit a site from enough lanes at once that holding one angle stops paying.
If one site keeps working for them they will keep going there, it really is not deeper than that, so start your round toward the site that has been winning.
Do not rotate off a man advantage you already have information on into a site you know nothing about, the numbers and the info are both worth more than the surprise.
The third time you see the same lurk in the same place it stops being a coincidence, say it out loud so the team can play around it.
Which side the enemy wall goes up on is the clearest read available, call it every round and watch whether they ever break the pattern.
Make a plan in the buy phase and commit to it, a round where you are still deciding at contact is a round you are playing a step behind.
You do not have to lurk just because you picked a sentinel, second entry with your utility already on the site is a real way to play the role.
Do not take the spike every round, carrying it turns every gunfight into a plant and you lose the reps that actually improve your aim.
Vary where you start the round, playing the same opening position every time is the easiest thing in the world to prepare against.
An ultimate you never press is worth nothing, spend it on a round you can still win rather than saving it for a perfect one that never arrives.
Play the same way at zero and ten as at ten and zero, letting the scoreline change how you sound is how a losable game becomes a lost one.
Keep the call simple enough that four other people can execute it, an overthought read nobody follows is worth less than an obvious one everybody does.
Spectre does 26 to the body inside 15 meters and 22 past it, so it wins the close fight and loses every long one.
Stinger drops from 27 to 23 past 15 meters, buy it to hold a choke, not to trade across a site.
Ghost holds 30 to the body all the way to 30 meters, which is why it out ranges every other pistol on an eco.
Sheriff does 55 to the body out to 30 meters, so on a save it beats a rifle at range if you hit the first shot.
Frenzy falls from 26 to 21 past 20 meters, so it is a close angle gun and never an answer to a rifle across the map.
Classic keeps 26 to the body out to 30 meters, so on a pistol round range matters far less than your first shot landing.
Bandit stays at 39 to the body all the way to 30 meters before it drops, which makes it the eco pistol that punishes a long hold.
Ares only drops from 30 to 28 past 30 meters, so its wall spam stays dangerous at almost any range.
Odin does 38 to the body inside 30 meters and 31 past it, and it shreds walls, so spam the common angle rather than peeking it.
Vandal does 40 to the body at every range on the map, so it is the one rifle whose value does not change when the fight gets long.
Guardian does 65 to the body at any range and two taps a full shield, so it punishes a long hold on a half buy.
Marshal does 101 to the body at every range, so one body and one pistol shot is a kill and you do not need the head.
Outlaw fires two shots before reloading and does 140 a body at any range, so it wins a double peek an Operator cannot.
Spread out before you commit, three players stacked in one choke tells them the site before you have taken a single duel.
A lurk only pays if it threatens the rotate, sitting in an empty corner where nobody walks is just playing four versus five.
A fake has to cost them something, if they do not spend utility or rotate a player then you announced your real site for free.
With a man advantage play slower, not faster, the extra player is worth more as patience than as a fifth body in the choke.
Do not spend the whole team utility on the entry, keep one smoke or flash for the moment they rotate in behind you.
Take space early and hold it, ground you own at forty seconds is ground you do not have to fight through at fifteen.
Once the spike is down the round is about time, so hold the angles that watch it and let them come to you.
Do not rotate off a site you already have numbers and information on, the man advantage and the read are both worth more than surprise.
Early aggression buys information once, doing it every round just donates a player to a team that now expects you.
Anchoring and rotating are two different jobs, decide which one you are doing before the barriers drop rather than halfway through the round.
Giving ground is not losing the site, falling back to a crossfire you can trade from beats dying alone at the choke.
Retake together and with utility, arriving one at a time is how a four versus two retake turns into a lost round.
If the round is lost, save the gun, one rifle kept is worth more than a heroic one versus four that was never going to land.
Watching the flank is a job, not a feeling, pick the angle that actually covers it and hold it rather than drifting back to the fight.
Which side their wall goes up on is the clearest read you get all round, call it every time and watch whether they ever break the pattern.
Count the bodies before you contest, two of you against four on site is a retake to set up, not a fight to take now.
